comparator.name: Communication Science
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 prospective programme overview (year-specific pages are indicative and may change)
comparator.sourceNotes: Official prospective pages display a complete 60 EC in each of three years. Year 1 has 60 EC compulsory; year 2 has 55 EC compulsory and 5 EC free choice; year 3 has 50 EC compulsory, including a 15 EC internship and a 15 EC thesis, plus 10 EC free choice. The two free-choice components remain uninstantiated. Zero-credit academic-language work is excluded. The current year-specific pages all say 2026–2027, so this is a documented illustrative three-year pathway rather than a guaranteed cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest response covers media functions, audience effects and empirical methods. The digital route is a distinct, evidenced concentration on social media and human-machine communication and differs by more than four substantive courses. Health and well-being is an evidenced application, but the available target evidence does not support another coherent 24-course communication curriculum without substituting biomedical content for media study.

ucr-1.text: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

notes.text: Radboud offers a sustained specialist communication-science sequence with credited empirical projects, a required internship and bachelor thesis. UCR combines media, rhetoric, psychology, research methods and digital systems but does not reproduce that entire specialist sequence.
